What is Spring Boot Actuator and why use it?

A sub-project that adds production-ready features through HTTP or JMX endpoints: health checks, metrics, app info, log level management, environment and bean inspection, and thread and heap dumps. You get observability without writing any code, Kubernetes probes, Prometheus metrics for Grafana dashboards and alerts, and faster troubleshooting in production, such as switching a package to DEBUG without a restart.
Which endpoints are enabled and exposed by default? How do you expose more?

Almost every endpoint is enabled (shutdown isn't), but over HTTP only /health is exposed. Enabled and exposed are separate settings. To expose more: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info,metrics,prometheus, or * for everything (not in production). JMX exposure is separate (management.endpoints.jmx.exposure.include).
How does /health decide UP or DOWN? How to add a custom check?

Every HealthIndicator bean contributes a component status. The StatusAggregator combines them in severity order (DOWN > OUT_OF_SERVICE > UP > UNKNOWN), so the worst one wins. The HTTP status follows: DOWN and OUT_OF_SERVICE return 503, UP returns 200. For a custom check, implement HealthIndicator (or the reactive ReactiveHealthIndicator) and return Health.up()/down().withDetail(...). Disable one with management.health.redis.enabled=false. Use health groups to build custom aggregates like readiness.
Liveness vs readiness probes — what goes where?

Liveness answers whether the app is broken and needs a restart. Keep external dependencies out of it, or a database outage will cause a cascade of restarts. Readiness answers whether the pod can take traffic; if not, it's removed from the load balancer. It can include the DB and cache. Boot tracks LivenessState and ReadinessState automatically: readiness turns on after startup and off during graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful). Add a startupProbe for apps that boot slowly.
What is Micrometer? Counter vs Gauge vs Timer?

Micrometer is a vendor-neutral metrics facade ("SLF4J for metrics") with dimensional, tagged metrics. You record through a MeterRegistry, and a registry implementation exports the data (Prometheus, Datadog, and so on). Counter: only increases (requests, errors). Gauge: a sampled current value (queue size). Timer: count, total time, max and optional percentiles or histograms (latency). DistributionSummary: a distribution of sizes or amounts.
How do you integrate Actuator with Prometheus and Grafana?

Add micrometer-registry-prometheus and expose the prometheus endpoint. Prometheus pulls (scrapes) /actuator/prometheus on an interval, and Grafana queries Prometheus with PromQL for dashboards (RPS, error rate, p95 latency, JVM heap, Hikari pool usage) and alerts. Enable percentiles-histogram for accurate latency quantiles across all instances. Add a common application tag so you can filter by service.
How do you change log levels at runtime?
Send POST /actuator/loggers/{logger.name} with {"configuredLevel":"DEBUG"}. Use null to reset it. It takes effect immediately with no restart. Secure this endpoint.
How do you create a custom actuator endpoint?

Annotate a bean with @Endpoint(id="x") and its methods with @ReadOperation (GET), @WriteOperation (POST) and @DeleteOperation (DELETE). Use @Selector for path segments. It's technology-agnostic, so the same endpoint works over HTTP and JMX. Then expose it with exposure.include.
How do you secure actuator endpoints?

Use a dedicated SecurityFilterChain with EndpointRequest.toAnyEndpoint(): permit health and info, and require a role for the rest. Run them on a separate management.server.port that isn't reachable from the internet. Keep the exposure list minimal and leave show-details: when-authorized. Boot 3 masks /env values by default (show-values). Never expose heapdump publicly.
What changed in Actuator with Spring Boot 3?

httptrace became httpexchanges. Env and configprops values are masked by default. Micrometer Observation API and Micrometer Tracing replace Spring Cloud Sleuth. @RestControllerEndpoint was deprecated in 3.3. Native-image support was added, along with an /sbom endpoint (3.3).
What is Spring Boot Admin?

A community project (codecentric) that provides a web UI on top of Actuator for many services. It shows health, metrics, logs, log levels, JVM details and notifications. Clients register directly or through service discovery.
How would you debug a production issue using Actuator?

Check /health to see which dependency is DOWN. Check /metrics for spikes in http.server.requests with status=5xx, saturation in hikaricp.connections.pending, and jvm.gc.pause. Switch the package logger to DEBUG through /loggers. Take a /threaddump to find blocked or deadlocked threads. Use /heapdump with Eclipse MAT for memory leaks. Use /info to confirm which build is deployed. Then correlate with traces and logs (traceId).
Enabled vs exposed vs access: what is the difference?

Access (or enabled before 3.4) decides whether the endpoint exists and what it permits. Exposure decides which technology publishes it, web or JMX. Both are needed. An endpoint with read-only access rejects write operations even if exposed.
Probes run on the management port, the app stopped accepting requests, but the pod still gets traffic. Why?

The management server has its own connector and thread pool, so it stays healthy while the main one is stuck. Enable management.endpoint.health.probes.add-additional-paths=true, and point probes at /livez and /readyz on the main port.
A gauge reports NaN after a while. Why?

Micrometer keeps a weak reference to the state object, so it does not stop garbage collection. If the object was local, it is collected, and the gauge returns NaN. Hold it in a long-lived field, or use the strong reference option Gauge.Builder.strongReference(true).
Why can you not average p95 across instances?

A percentile is not additive: two pods with p95 of 100 ms and 900 ms do not mean 500 ms overall, as it depends on request counts and distributions. Export histogram buckets, sum the buckets across pods, and compute the quantile from those in Prometheus.
How do traces connect across microservices?

The first service creates a trace id. Each HTTP or messaging client adds a traceparent header, and the next service continues that trace in a child span. Spans are exported to a backend such as Tempo, Jaeger or Zipkin. In Spring, this works when you use the auto-configured builders, and Micrometer Tracing is on the class path. @Async work needs context propagation.
Traces are missing for most requests. Is something broken?

Often no: the default sampling probability is 0.1, so 90% are not exported. Raise it in lower environments, or use tail-based sampling in an OpenTelemetry Collector, to keep all errors and slow traces while keeping cost under control.
Can a health check bring down production?

Yes. An expensive indicator hit by many probes adds load. A dependency included in liveness causes restart storms during an outage. A shared dependency in readiness can remove every pod at once, which turns a partial failure into a total one. Keep liveness internal, and include in readiness only what the instance cannot work without.
Which alerts would you set up for a Spring Boot REST service?

Use the RED signals from http.server.requests: the error rate (5xx ratio), latency (p95 or p99 from histogram buckets), and a traffic drop to near zero. Add saturation signals: hikaricp.connections.pending, heap usage after GC, thread pool queue size, and Kafka consumer lag where it applies. Finally, alert when the readiness probe fails or a pod restarts. Each alert should have a for duration and a runbook. Page only on user-facing symptoms, and send the rest to a ticket queue.
How do you see which version and commit is running in production?

Generate build-info.properties with the Boot build plugin and git.properties with the git-commit-id plugin. Expose the info endpoint. /actuator/info then shows the artifact version, build time, branch and commit id. Inject BuildProperties to log the version at startup, or to add it as a common metric tag. This makes it easy to compare metrics before and after a deployment.
Prometheus scraping vs pushing metrics with OTLP: what is the difference?

With pull (/actuator/prometheus), Prometheus discovers the targets and scrapes them. It is simple and shows target health ("up"), but it needs network access to every pod. With push (the OTLP registry), the app sends metrics to an OpenTelemetry Collector or a vendor backend. This works across network boundaries and for short-lived jobs, and it uses one protocol for metrics, traces and logs. Boot supports both through Micrometer registries. Choose according to your platform, and do not expose the scrape endpoint publicly.
Is Actuator available over JMX?

Yes, but JMX is off by default (spring.jmx.enabled=false since Boot 2.2). If you enable it, the endpoints exposed over JMX are set separately with management.endpoints.jmx.exposure.include. JMX helps with tools like JConsole or VisualVM, and in legacy environments. In containers, HTTP endpoints and Prometheus are the norm. If JMX is used remotely, it must be secured with authentication and TLS, because an open JMX port can allow remote code execution.
How do you monitor a @Scheduled or batch job?

Recent Spring versions record an observation for @Scheduled methods (tasks.scheduled.execution) when an ObservationRegistry is present. That gives duration and outcome. Add a LongTaskTimer to see jobs that are running now and how long they have run, and a gauge such as last_success_timestamp. Alert when time() - last_success_timestamp is too large, because a job that never runs produces no error metric at all.
